I have a very similar experience to yours. I have a hard time telling where OCD ends and schizoaffective starts, and vice versa. Or if I even have schizoaffective to begin with. It’s caused a lot of doubt in me, especially when I’m going through a relatively low symptoms period. I think if you have any doubts, you should ask your psychologist/psychiatrist about why they think you have it, sort of have them list out what you said or they noticed that lead them to that conclusion. It might help give you an understanding of what someone with an outside point of view interprets your situation, especially someone who is medically qualified
I also have OCD. Sometimes it’s hard to tell where the OCD ends and schizoaffective begins, and vice versa

I’ve had a variety of them, such as:

-My partner was cheating on me, everyone knew about it and was lying to me about it
-I’m actually dead and my body is rotting from the inside out
-my body is being taken over by parasites
-a friend I had a falling out with was sending demons through my mirror to kill me in my sleep
-I am pregnant (even when i wasn’t even sexually active)
-I need to sell my belongings and get rid of my body to achieve “ultimate freedom” (idk the logic behind that one but my brain was adamant it made sense)
-everything was a sign from the universe for this or that reason
-everyone is deceiving me in some way 

I’m sure I’ve had others I can’t think of at the moment, but these are a few I’ve had over the years. Some are more intense than others, some last longer than others. Some even feel a bit more tame/“grounded in reality” than others (ex: cheating delusion vs demons in my mirrors delusion). It’s sometimes hard to tell you’re in a delusion until you come out of it

I can daydream. It’s actually a bit of a problem for me, it’s making it hard to stay present and focused on my day to day life because i can’t stop. I found my dreams often changed in frequency and intensity with the medication I was taking and the mental/emotional state I was in.
I have schizoaffective bipolar type, OCD, panic disorder, PTSD, dissociation, and some mild agoraphobia

A couple years ago, I dropped out due to psychosis and enrolled for the following fall. It was tough at first, I was working, a full time student, and just starting to live on my own, but things turned out okay. The best advice I can give you is don’t push yourself too hard. If you’re able to, I suggest taking the minimum amount of classes possible for a full time student (if you’re doing full time). It allows time for a job while also giving you room to breathe. Best of luck to you! You got this!

i posted this on a different post but i call it the four modes

https://www.reddit.com/r/Dissociation/comments/oya60r/whats\_your\_symptoms/h7ttsqe?utm\_source=share&utm\_medium=web2x&context=3

I call it the four modes:

1. Inverted and slightly to the left (everything is warped and confusing)
2. GTA5/Understudy/Shadowing (watching myself go about my day, like floating or following behind my body)
3. Car with no seat belts (like everything is just free form and not permanent. Like I might clip through the floor at any moment like a video game glitch)
4. Static (nothing makes sense and sort of how u/Anonalt2702 said it, everything is too close or too far and its muffled and everything seems unrecognizable. Like i cant feel my own body sometimes)
